title: Listening & Reading
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tentang liburan dan struktur past simple untuk bertanya dan menjawab tentang liburan di masa lalu.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 75-77
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to understand and identify additional key vocabulary about places and activities on vacation.
Learners will listen and understand people talking about vacations in the past.
Learners will read and understand a letter about a vacation.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures in Listening A on Student Book page 75.
Tell them that they need to listen and circle the vocabulary word that matches the picture.

Before listening, practice pronunciation of the words in task A. The teacher says the two vocabulary choices given for each number, for example, “Number 1. a village. a villain.”, and students repeat them aloud.
Play audio 9.3. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check students’ understanding.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner and then check the answers together.

Play audio again and ask students to write down the sentences they hear in their notebooks (this is a simple dictation activity). Then show the audio script and ask students to correct their sentences.
This activity is for pronunciation practice.

Play audio 9.4 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly (a village, a city, the forest, a hotel, bought souvenirs, went sightseeing), and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
In order to make vocabulary drilling more interesting, students could be guided to drill using different emotions (e.g. excited or tired) or voices.
Ask students to look at listening task C and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Tell students that they need to listen and write the letter in the box that correctly completes each sentence (match the beginnings 1–6 with the endings a–f).
Read the beginnings and the endings of the sentences aloud together as a class to prepare students for the listening task.
Play audio 9.5. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, play the audio again, and then check the answers together. Write the correct answers on the board.
Read the complete sentences aloud as a class, or in pairs (e.g. “Oliver went to a big city and saw many tall buildings, malls, and lots of people walking around.”).
Ask students to look at the pictures on Student Book page 76-77.
Ask the class, “What can you see on the page?” and some specific questions about the pictures, for example, “How many people can you see?”, “Where are they?”
Giving some personal questions is also suggested to make it more relatable to students, for example, “Have you ever gone on vacation with your grandparents?”
Ask students to look at task A on Student Book page 76.
Read the vocabulary (went to an amusement park, took photos, tried local food, saw animals) and the definitions aloud, and ask students to repeat them after you.
Elicit from students what they can see in each picture.
They need to match the words to their definitions and to the correct pictures by writing the matching letters and numerals.
Do the first activity together as a class to make sure students understand what to do. Check the answers as a class and drill the pronunciation of the key vocabulary.
Ask students to look at task B on Student Book page 76.
Put students in pairs and ask them to discuss the questions together (e.g. “What can you do at an amusement park?”, “Do you like trying local food? Why or why not?”).
Give students 3-5 minutes to complete the task.
Then ask some students to share their answers with the class. Answers will vary because these questions require students' own personal responses.
Tell students that they will listen and read the letter “Ben’s Great Vacation”. Play audio 9.6 and ask them to read the text silently.
Next, play the audio again and ask students to read the text aloud, following the audio. Ask if there are any questions about the language in the text.

As a way to make the reading session more engaging, teachers could divide the class into several groups and assign each group to read one paragraph alternately in different ways (e.g. loudly or quietly).
Ask students to look at task D on Student Book page 77.
Read sentences a-f aloud together as a class. Tell students that they need to put these sentences in order from 1-6 according to the events in Ben’s letter.
Tell students to read the text again to help them do this.
The first question can be done together as a class to make sure students know what to do. Then, they can complete the task in pairs or by themselves.
Ask students to check their answers with a friend.
Check the answers as a class. Write the answers on the board and ask students to show where they found each answer in the text.
Now ask students to look at task E on page 77.

Instruct them to discuss the questions in groups of three or four students (e.g. “What are some things you did on your last vacation?”, “How did you get there?”, “How did you feel during your last vacation?”).
Remind students to answer using the past simple (e.g. “We took a bus to the city.”).
After about 6-8 minutes, elicit some answers for each question from each group.
This activity could be done if there is more time.
Ask students to write a short letter (around 60-80 words) to a friend or family member about a vacation that they took.
Their letter should include where they went, how they got there, where they stayed, and 2-3 activities they did on the vacation.
Tell students to look at Ben’s letter on Student Book pages 76-77 as an example of what to write.
Give students a few minutes to brainstorm ideas in pairs, then let them write their letter in their notebooks.
Put students in pairs and tell them to read their letters aloud to each other. Ask 2-3 students to read their letter to the class.
Wrap up the class by asking the students which place from today’s lesson (a village, a city, the forest, an amusement park) they would like to visit on their next vacation, and why.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: ketepatan jawaban tugas listening (menomori/menjodohkan/melengkapi).
Pertanyaan pemahaman bacaan (literal & inferensial) dan pembahasan bersama.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
